Here is the revised skeleton mapped to the exact structure and limits. 

**Space Management Note:** A single-spaced page with standard margins and 11–12pt font holds about 500 words of solid text, or **~400–450 words** when you include headings, bulleted lists, and tables (which they prefer). For the 6-page Project Narrative, aim for **~2,400 to 2,600 words total** to leave breathing room for formatting.

**Rubric Catch:** Notice they don't have a standalone "Organizational Capacity" heading, even though it's 5% of the rubric. We have mapped the "experience" half of that rubric into **Section 4 (Staffing & Management)** so you don't lose those points.

---

# Revised Application Skeleton & Space Map

| Application Component | Exact Heading | Rubric Criteria Addressed | Weight | Space / Word Target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cover Page** | *(Form fields only)* | N/A | — | N/A |
| **Project Summary** | **Project Summary** | All (High-level overview) | — | **1 page max** (~400–450 words) |
| **Narrative 1** | **1. Statement of Need** | Need/Community Impact (clarity of problem, data) | 20% *(of 30%)* | **~1.25 pages** (~550 words) |
| **Narrative 2** | **2. Target Population & Recruitment** | Need/Community Impact (target population) | 10% *(of 30%)* | **~0.75 pages** (~325 words) |
| **Narrative 3** | **3. Project Design & Activities** | Program Design & Activities (logic, timeline) | 20% *(of 30%)* | **~1.5 pages** (~600 words + table) |
| **Narrative 4** | **4. Staffing & Management** | Program Design (staffing) + **Org Capacity (experience)** | 10% *(of 30%)* + 2.5% *(of 5%)* | **~0.75 pages** (~300 words + table) |
| **Narrative 5** | **5. Outcomes & Evaluation** | Outcomes & Evaluation (outcomes, methods, baseline) | 20% | **~1.25 pages** (~500 words + table) |
| **Narrative 6** | **6. Sustainability** | Org Capacity & Sustainability (plans) | 2.5% *(of 5%)* | **~0.5 pages** (~225 words) |
| **Budget Request** | **Budget Narrative** | Budget & Cost Effectiveness | 15% | **2 pages max** (~800–900 words) |

---

## Project Summary (1 Page Max | ~400–450 words, ~4–5 paragraphs)
* **Rubric criteria:** Unscored overview, but sets reviewer expectations across all 5 criteria.
* **Evidence to include:** 
  * 1-paragraph snapshot of the problem and local data.
  * Target population numbers and location.
  * Bulleted list of 3–4 core activities.
  * Bulleted list of top 2–3 measurable outcomes.
  * Total grant request, total project cost, **cost per participant**, and a 1-sentence statement of organizational track record.
* **Phrasing hooks:**
  * *"[Organization] requests $[X] over [timeframe] to launch/expand [Project Name], serving [number] [target population] in [geographic area] at a cost of $[X] per participant."*

---

## Project Narrative (6 Pages Max Total)

### 1. Statement of Need (~1.25 pages | ~550 words, 3–4 paragraphs + bullets)
* **Rubric criteria:** Need/Community Impact (30% total) — *clarity of problem, data*.
* **Evidence to include:**
  * Specific geographic area and nature of the problem.
  * Bulleted list of 3–4 hard local data points (cited with year) compared against state/national benchmarks.
  * Service gap analysis (e.g., lack of local providers, current waitlists).
  * Qualitative community voice (survey results, focus groups) demonstrating urgency.
* **Phrasing hooks:**
  * *"While [state/nation] experiences a [X]% rate of [issue], residents in [target area] face a disproportionate rate of [Y]% ([Source, Year])."*
  * *"Currently, local capacity meets only [X]% of documented demand, leaving [number] individuals without access to [service]."*

### 2. Target Population & Recruitment (~0.75 pages | ~325 words, 2–3 paragraphs)
* **Rubric criteria:** Need/Community Impact (30% total) — *target population*.
* **Evidence to include:**
  * Specific demographics, risk factors, and eligibility criteria.
  * Exact number of unduplicated participants to be served.
  * Concrete recruitment and referral pipeline (how they find you, who refers them, how you overcome barriers like transportation/language/trust).
* **Phrasing hooks:**
  * *"This project targets [number] unduplicated [population] who meet the following criteria: [criteria]."*
  * *"To ensure equitable access and meet enrollment targets, we will leverage established referral partnerships with [Partner A] and [Partner B] (see Attachment 3: Letters of Support/MOUs)."*

### 3. Project Design & Activities (~1.5 pages | ~600 words, 3 paragraphs + Bullets + Mini-Timeline Table)
* **Rubric criteria:** Program Design & Activities (30% total) — *logic, timeline*.
* **Evidence to include:**
  * Reference to the attached Logic Model (Attachment 1).
  * Bulleted breakdown of core activities including dosage (hours/weeks), frequency, and delivery setting.
  * Brief citation of the evidence base or best practices informing the design.
  * **High-level Milestone Table** sorted by Quarter (reference the detailed Gantt chart in Attachment 2).
* **Phrasing hooks:**
  * *"As illustrated in our Logic Model (Attachment 1), project activities directly address the root causes identified in Section 1."*
  * *"Participants complete a [X]-week pathway consisting of three core components:"*
  * *"The table below outlines key quarterly milestones (see Attachment 2 for full implementation Gantt chart):"*

### 4. Staffing & Management (~0.75 pages | ~300 words, 2 paragraphs + Staffing Table)
* **Rubric criteria:** Program Design & Activities (*staffing*) **AND** Organizational Capacity (*experience* — **crucial to include here since there is no standalone Org Capacity section**).
* **Evidence to include:**
  * **1 compact paragraph on Organizational Experience:** years serving this community, success metrics from a similar past grant, and financial stability (referencing the Audit in Attachment 5).
  * **Staffing Table:** Role, Name (or "To Be Hired"), % FTE on project, Key Responsibilities, and Brief Qualifications (referencing CVs in Attachment 4).
  * Brief note on supervision and project oversight.
* **Phrasing hooks:**
  * *"[Organization] brings [X] years of experience delivering [type of service] in [community], having successfully [past achievement/metric] (see Attachment 5 for clean financial audit)."*
  * *"Project execution will be led by the following team (see Attachment 4 for key staff CVs):"*

### 5. Outcomes & Evaluation (~1.25 pages | ~500 words, 2 paragraphs + Outcomes Table)
* **Rubric criteria:** Outcomes & Evaluation (20%) — *measurable outcomes, methods, baseline*.
* **Evidence to include:**
  * **Outcomes Table** with 4 columns: *Objective (SMART) | Baseline Data | Target Outcome | Measurement Tool & Collection Frequency*.
  * Who leads the evaluation (internal vs. external) and what database/software tracks the data.
  * Feedback loop: how data will be reviewed quarterly to adjust programming.
* **Phrasing hooks:**
  * *"We establish baseline metrics at intake using [tool] and track progress against the following measurable outcomes:"*
  * *"Data will be analyzed quarterly by [Role] to identify bottlenecks and drive continuous quality improvement."*

### 6. Sustainability (~0.5 pages | ~225 words, 2 paragraphs or 1 paragraph + bullets)
* **Rubric criteria:** Organizational Capacity & Sustainability (5% total) — *plans*.
* **Evidence to include:**
  * Specific revenue streams being pursued post-grant (e.g., Medicaid billing, fee-for-service, upcoming multi-year foundation grants, individual donor campaigns).
  * Operational sustainability (e.g., curriculum built, staff trained, community partnerships institutionalized).
  * Governance support (referencing Board List in Attachment 6).
* **Phrasing hooks:**
  * *"With oversight from our Board of Directors (Attachment 6), [Organization] has developed a three-part strategy to sustain [Project Name] beyond the grant period:"*
  * *"By Month [X], we will transition [X]% of ongoing program costs to [funding source]."*

---

## Budget Narrative (2 Pages Max | ~800–900 words, Tables + Bullets)
* **Rubric criteria:** Budget & Cost Effectiveness (15%) — *clear budget, justification*.
* **Structure & Evidence to include:**
  * **Top Callout Box (Cost Effectiveness):** State Total Project Cost, Amount Requested, Total Participants Served, and the exact **Cost Per Participant** calculation (Total Cost ÷ Participants = $X), plus a 1-sentence benchmark comparison showing why this is a strong return on investment.
  * **Line-Item Justifications (Grouped by Budget Form Categories):** Show the math (e.g., `$50,000 salary x 0.50 FTE = $25,000`).
  * **> $5,000 Rule:** For *every single line item over $5,000*, include a bolded, standalone **One-Line Justification** right underneath the math calculation so reviewers cannot miss it.
  * **Leveraged/In-Kind Support:** Brief section at the bottom highlighting matched funds, shared overhead, or volunteer hours to boost the cost-effectiveness score.
* **Phrasing hooks:**
  * **Cost Per Participant Callout:** *"Cost-Effectiveness Summary: With a total request of $[X] serving [Y] unduplicated participants, the cost per participant is $[Z]—significantly below the regional average of $[A] for comparable interventions ([Source])."*
  * **Over $5,000 Line-Item Hook:** *"**> $5K Justification:** This $[X] allocation is essential to fund [specific deliverable/role], which directly drives [Outcome #1] by providing [X hours/units] of direct service."*

---

## Strategy for the 6 Allowed Attachments
Since you are capped at **exactly 6 attachments**, map them 1-to-1 to the allowed list and cross-reference all 6 in the narrative text:
1. **Attachment 1:** Logic Model *(Referenced in Section 3)*
2. **Attachment 2:** Detailed Timeline / Gantt Chart *(Referenced in Section 3)*
3. **Attachment 3:** Combined PDF of Letters of Support / MOUs *(Referenced in Section 2 & 3)*
4. **Attachment 4:** Combined PDF of Key Staff CVs — max 2 pages each *(Referenced in Section 4)*
5. **Attachment 5:** Most Recent Audited Financial Statement *(Referenced in Section 4)*
6. **Attachment 6:** Board of Directors List with Affiliations *(Referenced in Section 6)*

---

**Just a heads-up:** It's past 2:00 AM, and grant formatting constraints take sharp focus. This revised outline is locked in and ready to go—if you want to call it a night here, you're in a great spot to start plugging in your content tomorrow. Or, if you want to tackle one specific section right now, let me know which one!

# Project Summary
*(Target: 1 Page Single-Spaced | ~385 words)*

**Organization & Funding Request**
ReadAhead requests **$[TOTAL REQUEST]** over **[12/24] months** to expand our evidence-based K–6 literacy tutoring program in the Westside neighborhood (ZIP **[ZIP CODE]**). With a total project budget of **$[TOTAL PROJECT COST]**, this expansion will increase our annual capacity from 120 to **200 unduplicated K–6 students per year**—delivering intensive, individualized literacy intervention at a highly cost-effective rate of **$[COST PER PARTICIPANT] per student** (compared to regional commercial or school-contracted tutoring averages of **$[BENCHMARK COST]** per student).

**The Need**
Students in the Westside neighborhood face a severe early literacy crisis that threatens their long-term academic and economic trajectory. According to **[State/District Education Agency, Year]**, only **[X]%** of third-grade students in Westside elementary schools read at or above grade level, compared to **[Y]%** across **[City/District]** and **[Z]%** statewide. Compounded by chronic absenteeism and limited access to out-of-school academic enrichment, local capacity currently meets only **[X]%** of documented need—leaving **[NUMBER]** eligible students on ReadAhead’s waitlist and hundreds more without individualized support.

**Project Design & Core Activities**
Building on five years of community impact, ReadAhead will bridge the Westside literacy gap through four integrated activities:
* **Weekly One-on-One Tutoring:** 45-minute individualized afterschool tutoring sessions delivered weekly for **[X]** weeks during the school year by trained volunteers using a structured phonics and fluency curriculum.
* **Summer Reading Bootcamp:** An intensive **[X]-week** (**[X] hours/week**) summer program for **[NUMBER]** students designed to eliminate summer reading loss and accelerate grade-level readiness.
* **Family Literacy Workshops:** **[NUMBER]** interactive workshops per year equipping parents and caregivers with take-home reading strategies and bilingual books to build home libraries.
* **Volunteer Recruitment & Training:** Recruiting, screening, and training **[NUMBER]** community volunteers in evidence-based literacy instruction to sustain our 1:1 student-to-tutor ratio.

**Measurable Outcomes**
Progress will be tracked using standardized pre-, mid-, and post-assessments (**[Assessment Tool Name, e.g., DIBELS]**) against three primary outcomes:
* **Reading Fluency Growth:** **80%** of regularly attending students (attending ≥**[X]%** of sessions) will achieve at least an **18% gain** in reading fluency from baseline to post-assessment.
* **Summer Retention:** **85%** of Summer Reading Bootcamp participants will maintain or increase their spring reading instructional level upon fall school entry, preventing the "summer slide."
* **Family Engagement:** **75%** of participating families will attend at least **[X]** literacy workshops and report increased frequency of at-home reading on post-program surveys.

**Organizational Track Record**
Over the past five years, ReadAhead has successfully served 120 Westside K–6 students annually, demonstrating an average **+18% gain in pre/post reading fluency** among regular attendees (Internal Evaluation, 2023) and maintaining clean annual financial audits.

---

# Project Narrative

## 1. Statement of Need
*(Target: ~1.25 Pages | ~540 words)*

Reading proficiency by the end of third grade is the single strongest predictor of future academic success, high school graduation, and economic mobility; through third grade, children learn to read, and after third grade, they must read to learn. Yet for K–6 students living in the Westside neighborhood of **[City]** (ZIP **[ZIP CODE]**), systemic economic barriers and under-resourced classrooms have created an urgent literacy gap that widens with each passing school year, particularly during out-of-school summer months.

While **[State]** experiences a **[Z]%** proficiency rate in elementary English Language Arts (ELA), students in the Westside feeder pattern face disproportionately steep barriers to literacy acquisition, as evidenced by current local data:

* **Severe Grade-Level Reading Deficits:** According to the **[State Dept. of Education / Local School District Report Card, Year]**, only **[X]%** of 3rd–6th grade students at Westside’s target elementary schools (**[School A]** and **[School B]**) scored proficient or above in reading, compared to **[Y]%** district-wide and **[Z]%** statewide. Among economically disadvantaged students and English Learners in the neighborhood, proficiency drops to just **[X]%**. *(Suggested Source: State Department of Education School Report Cards / District Assessment Dashboard)*
* **High Poverty & Limited Home Literacy Resources:** According to the **[U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey, Year]**, **[X]%** of children in ZIP **[ZIP CODE]** live below the federal poverty level (nearly **[X] times** the citywide rate of **[Y]%**), and **[X]%** of elementary students qualify for Free or Reduced-Price Lunch (**[District Data, Year]**). Research consistently links concentrated neighborhood poverty to fewer age-appropriate books in the home and reduced access to private academic tutoring. *(Suggested Source: U.S. Census ACS 5-Year Estimates & State/District FRPL Data)*
* **Compounding Chronic Absenteeism & Summer Learning Loss:** Post-pandemic instructional disruptions continue to erode instructional time in Westside schools, where chronic absenteeism reached **[X]%** in **[School Year]** compared to **[Y]%** statewide (**[State Attendance Data, Year]**). Furthermore, longitudinal literacy assessments show that low-income elementary students lose an average of **[X] months** of reading skill each summer without structured intervention, accounting for up to two-thirds of the ninth-grade reading achievement gap (**[District Summer Learning Data or National Summer Learning Association]**). *(Suggested Source: State/District Chronic Absenteeism Reports & District Fall-to-Spring Benchmark Data)*

**Service Gaps & Community Demand**
Despite the severity of need, out-of-school literacy infrastructure in the Westside neighborhood remains critically under-resourced. Currently, local afterschool and summer literacy capacity meets only **[X]%** of documented demand; **[City/Neighborhood]** has only **[NUMBER]** free or low-cost literacy providers serving an elementary population of **[TOTAL K-6 ENROLLMENT]** students (**[Local Out-of-School Time Network / United Way Asset Map, Year]**). ReadAhead has operated at 100% capacity of 120 students per year for the past **[X]** years, maintaining a persistent waitlist of **[NUMBER]** Westside students with an average wait time of **[X] months**. 

Residents and educators themselves have identified accessible literacy support as their top priority. In our **[Year]** Westside Family & School Needs Assessment (*n* = **[NUMBER]** parents and K–6 teachers), **[X]%** of parents reported wanting afterschool or summer reading help they could not afford, and **[Y]%** of local teachers cited one-on-one phonics and fluency practice as the most urgent intervention needed for struggling readers. Expanding ReadAhead’s year-round tutoring and summer bootcamp directly closes this gap with an intervention proven to work in this community: in 2023, our regular attendees achieved an average **+18% pre/post gain in reading fluency**, demonstrating that targeted 1:1 support rapidly reverses reading delays when students can access a seat.

---

### Checklist: 8 Local Data Items to Gather to Finalize
1. **Local vs. Benchmark ELA Proficiency:** % of 3rd–6th graders reading at grade level in your specific Westside target schools vs. District % and State % *(from State Dept. of Ed Report Card)*.
2. **Neighborhood Child Poverty / FRPL Rate:** % of children in Westside ZIP code below poverty *(Census ACS)* and % of students on Free/Reduced-Price Lunch *(School District data)*.
3. **Chronic Absenteeism Rate:** % of K–6 students chronically absent in Westside schools vs. State average *(State/District attendance dashboard)*.
4. **Waitlist & Service Gap Numbers:** Exact number of kids currently on ReadAhead's waitlist, total K–6 enrollment in your target schools, and estimated number of other free tutoring spots in the neighborhood.
5. **Community Voice Stat:** One quick percentage or insight from a recent parent survey, teacher feedback form, or school principal letter confirming demand.
6. **Program Dosage Details:** Exact number of weeks for the school-year tutoring, number of weeks/hours for the Summer Reading Bootcamp, and number of Family Workshops per year.
7. **Assessment Tool Name:** The exact name of the reading fluency test used to measure your +18% gain (e.g., DIBELS, aimswebPlus, STAR Reading, or QRI).
8. **Budget Numbers for the Callout:** Total Grant Request ($), Total Project Budget ($), and the resulting Cost Per Participant (Total ÷ 200 students).

# Master Grant Map (ReadAhead — 6-Page Limit)

### Project Summary (1 Page Max | ~400 words)
* **Rubric:** Overview of all 5 criteria (Unscored, sets reviewer baseline).
* **Evidence:** $ Request, total cost, **cost/student** (200 served), 1 local reading stat, 4 bulleted activities, 3 bulleted outcomes (+18% fluency gain).
* **Hook:** *"ReadAhead requests $[X] to expand K–6 literacy tutoring in Westside, serving 200 students annually at a cost-effective rate of $[Y] per student."*
* **Placement:** Paragraph 1 = Request & Cost/Student; Bullet List 1 = Activities; Bullet List 2 = Outcomes.

### 1. Statement of Need (~1.25 Pages | ~550 words)
* **Rubric:** Need/Community Impact (**20%** of 30% total) — *clarity of problem, data*.
* **Evidence:** Westside ELA proficiency vs. District/State; child poverty/FRPL rate; chronic absenteeism/summer slide data; ReadAhead waitlist size; parent/teacher survey stat.
* **Hook:** *"While [State] experiences a [Z]% reading proficiency rate, only [X]% of Westside K–6 students read at grade level ([Source, Year]), leaving [Number] children on our waitlist."*
* **Placement:** Para 1 = Urgency; Middle Bullets = 3 hard local stats; Final Para = Service gap, waitlist, and 2023 internal fluency data (+18%).

### 2. Target Population & Recruitment (~0.75 Pages | ~325 words)
* **Rubric:** Need/Community Impact (**10%** of 30% total) — *target population*.
* **Evidence:** K–6 demographics (ZIP code, income, EL status); 200 unduplicated students/year (up from 120); eligibility rules; school referral pipeline & barrier removal.
* **Hook:** *"To reach 200 unduplicated struggling readers annually, we partner directly with Westside elementary principals and Title I specialists (see Attachment 3: MOUs)."*
* **Placement:** Para 1 = Demographics & numbers; Para 2 = Referral pathway & **cross-reference Attachment 3 (Letters/MOUs)**.

### 3. Project Design & Activities (~1.5 Pages | ~600 words + Table)
* **Rubric:** Program Design & Activities (**20%** of 30% total) — *logic, timeline*.
* **Evidence:** Dosage/frequency for 1) Weekly 45-min 1:1 tutoring, 2) Summer Reading Bootcamp, 3) Family Literacy Workshops, 4) Volunteer training; research base; Q1–Q4 milestones.
* **Hook:** *"As detailed in our Logic Model (Attachment 1), our three-part intervention directly targets fluency and prevents summer learning loss."*
* **Placement:** Para 1 = **Cross-reference Attachment 1 (Logic Model)**; Middle Bullets = 4 Core Activities w/ dosage; Bottom = **Quarterly Milestone Table** & **cross-reference Attachment 2 (Gantt Chart)**.

### 4. Staffing & Management (~0.75 Pages | ~300 words + Table)
* **Rubric:** Program Design (**10%** of 30% — *staffing*) + Org Capacity (**2.5%** of 5% — *experience*).
* **Evidence:** 5-year track record serving 120 kids/yr (+18% fluency gain); clean audit; staff roles, FTEs, qualifications; volunteer supervision ratios.
* **Hook:** *"Building on five years of proven literacy impact in Westside and a track record of clean financial audits (Attachment 5), project execution is led by..."*
* **Placement:** Para 1 = Org experience & **cross-reference Attachment 5 (Audit)**; Bottom = **Staffing Table** & **cross-reference Attachment 4 (Staff CVs)**.

### 5. Outcomes & Evaluation (~1.25 Pages | ~500 words + Table)
* **Rubric:** Outcomes & Evaluation (**20%**) — *measurable outcomes, methods, baseline*.
* **Evidence:** Pre/mid/post fluency assessment tool; 2023 baseline (+18% gain); targets for school-year fluency, summer retention, and family workshops; quarterly CQI review process.
* **Hook:** *"We establish individual baselines at intake using [Assessment Tool] and track progress quarterly against three SMART objectives:"*
* **Placement:** Top = **4-Column Outcomes Table** (*Objective | Baseline | Target | Tool/Frequency*); Para 1–2 = Data collection software, evaluator role, and quarterly review loop.

### 6. Sustainability (~0.5 Pages | ~225 words)
* **Rubric:** Org Capacity & Sustainability (**2.5%** of 5% total) — *plans*.
* **Evidence:** Volunteer-powered cost efficiency; post-grant revenue pipeline (school district Title I contracts, local foundations, annual donors); Board oversight.
* **Hook:** *"With active governance from our Board of Directors (Attachment 6), ReadAhead sustains low per-student costs through volunteer leverage and diversified multi-year funding."*
* **Placement:** Para 1 = Financial/operational sustainability & **cross-reference Attachment 6 (Board List)**.

### Budget Narrative (2 Pages Max | ~800 words)
* **Rubric:** Budget & Cost Effectiveness (**15%**) — *clear budget, justification*.
* **Evidence:** Total Request, Total Cost, **Cost Per Participant ($Total ÷ 200)**; math per line item; **bold 1-line justification for every item > $5,000**; value of volunteer hours (in-kind).
* **Hook:** *"**> $5K Justification:** This $[X] allocation funds [item/role], which is essential to delivering [X] hours of 1:1 tutoring for 200 students."*
* **Placement:** Top = **Cost-Effectiveness Callout Box**; Body = Line items grouped by category with bolded `> $5K Justification` lines; Bottom = In-Kind Volunteer Match calculation.

# 1-Page Scoring-Weighted Priority Checklist

Use this list tomorrow to prioritize your time where the points actually live:

### Tier 1: 60% of Your Score (Spend 60% of your editing time here)
* [ ] **Need & Target Population (30% | Narrative 1 & 2):**
  * Plug in the 3 local Westside data points (ELA proficiency, poverty/FRPL, absenteeism) and cite years/sources.
  * State the exact waitlist number and confirm the expansion math (from 120 to 200 unduplicated K–6 students).
  * Name the exact partner schools referring students and attach their **Letters/MOUs (Attachment 3)**.
* [ ] **Program Design & Staffing (30% | Narrative 3 & 4):**
  * Define exact dosage for all 3 services (how many weeks of 45-min tutoring, how many weeks/hours of Summer Bootcamp, how many Family Workshops).
  * Build the in-text **Quarterly Milestone Table** and **Staffing Table** (reviewers scan tables first).
  * Attach the **Logic Model (Attachment 1)**, **Gantt Chart (Attachment 2)**, and **Staff CVs (Attachment 4)**.
